title: POC scoping: Data handling & benchmarks - Everwell Health
next_steps: Redwood: share Security & SOC2 docs and KMS integration guide by 2026-07-17
Redwood SE: share benchmark script and sample load profile by 2026-07-20
Everwell: provide 2 sample datasets (redacted + raw with PII mapping) and approved PII handling policy by 2026-07-22
Schedule pilot kickoff/workshop (2 hours) week of 2026-07-27
action_items: Maya Chen: Send POC pricing & pilot terms (incl. Dedicated vs Hosted options) — due 2026-07-17
Arjun Patel: Share JMeter/locust benchmark script + expected metrics and runbook — due 2026-07-20
Terry Huang (Everwell): Confirm which fields are considered PII and provide redaction rules doc — due 2026-07-22
Laura Gomez: Provide a 10k-record sample and a 100k-record anonymized sample for throughput test — due 2026-07-22
Jordan Li: Book pilot kickoff on calendar and send invite — due 2026-07-18
summary: POC scoping focused on how Everwell wants Redwood to handle PII during a 4-week pilot: redaction, minimal prompt storage, retention settings, and logging. Discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput, accuracy/regression thresholds), workload sizing for benchmarks, and timeline for delivery and kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm maya from Redwood, arjun our SE will cover the technical bits.
[00:12] Laura Gomez: Thanks, yeah we're excited; main goal is to validate data handling and perf for a triage assistant.
[00:25] Arjun Patel: Great; high level today we want to capture success criteria, what PII means for you, retention, and the benchmark shape. I'll ask a few questions about workload and then propose a pilot plan.
[00:40] Dr. Amit Rao: sounds good. security is big for us — we need to know what logs you keep, is raw prompt stored, and how keys are managed.
[00:54] Maya Chen: absolutely. quick note, transcription may have small errors. we'll follow up with docs.
[01:05] Terry Huang: for Everwell, PII includes patient names, MRNs, dates of birth, and free-text that could contain PHI. we prefer redaction at ingest and minimal prompt storage.
[01:22] Arjun Patel: ok, two primary options: redaction before sending (customer-side) or server-side redaction via a redaction webhook. we support both; server-side redaction logs masked copies but you can opt out of storing original prompts.
[01:41] Sofia Marin: what does opt out mean exactly? do requests still hit logs for debugging?
[01:49] Arjun Patel: good question — opt-out means we do not persist full prompt text to long-term logs. short-term ephemeral traces (48–72 hrs) for troubleshooting are available with access controls, or can be disabled entirely in Private deployments.
[02:10] Dr. Amit Rao: KMS integration? we need envelope encryption and customer-managed keys.
[02:16] Maya Chen: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can use our managed keys but for Everwell we recommended either Dedicated with CMK or Private deployment for full control.
[02:33] Laura Gomez: latency targets — we need median latency under 300ms for short prompts and 95th under 900ms. cost is also a factor.
[02:43] Arjun Patel: noted. for the POC we propose to run two benchmark profiles: a small prompt profile (avg 40 tokens, 4k requests over 1 hour) and a heavy profile (avg 200 tokens, bursty 1k rpm sustained over 30 minutes). we'll measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:06] Sofia Marin: how will you simulate our traffic shape? we have a mix of background async queries and interactive chat.
[03:14] Arjun Patel: we can parameterize the locust script to model both. we'll include KV cache warmup steps to approximate real-world cache hit rates.
[03:26] Laura Gomez: about prompt storage — do you store user prompts with model outputs? we have to avoid storing raw prompts tied to patient identifiers.
[03:36] Maya Chen: default hosted stores prompt+response for debugging and quality, retention 30 days; but you can configure retention shorter or disable storing raw prompt text. Dedicated/Private gives you full control.
[03:52] Terry Huang: audit logs — we need immutable logs of who accessed what and when, with export for audits.
[03:58] Jordan Li: Redwood's audit logging supports export to S3 and SIEM integrations, and logs can be retained per your policy. for POC we can enable 90-day retention and provide an export.
[04:12] Dr. Amit Rao: we also care about model drift/regression checks — if output quality drops after quantization we need alerts.
[04:21] Arjun Patel: our Optimize toolkit can run evals against a golden prompt set and raise regression alerts. we can attach your evals and set thresholds for acceptance.
[04:33] Laura Gomez: success criteria: 1) latency p50 <300ms p95 <900ms on small profile, 2) throughput target of 1k concurrent requests sustained for 15 minutes without errors, 3) redaction policy enforced (no stored PHI in hosted logs), and 4) no >5% quality regression on golden prompts.
[04:56] Maya Chen: perfect — we'll write that up as acceptance criteria.
[05:04] Sofia Marin: whats the expected timeline for pilot?
[05:09] Maya Chen: we propose 4 weeks: week 0 prep & data exchange, week 1 infra setup & small benchmark, week 2 full benchmark and tuning, week 3 evaluation and final report. kickoff next week would target completion by mid-aug.
[05:28] Laura Gomez: can you run the POC on dedicated infra? we prefer isolation for PHI.
[05:33] Maya Chen: yes Dedicated is recommended and we'll provide guidance on minimum capacity; approximate estimate: 1x A10G or equivalent for the small profile, 2x for heavy profiles depending on concurrency — SE will finalize sizing after we see sample payloads.
[05:52] Arjun Patel: some gotchas — quantized models can reduce memory but sometimes affect tail latencies; we'll include quantization profiles and perf tradeoffs in the report.
[06:04] Dr. Amit Rao: what about prompt caching? if we cache prefixes does that store anything we should worry about?
[06:11] Arjun Patel: cache stores KV material in memory; it does not persist prompts. however cache entries may be logged in traces; we'll ensure those traces are masked for PHI.
[06:25] Terry Huang: and retention settings — we need to cap log retention to 90 days and have the ability to purge particular records on request.
[06:33] Jordan Li: yes we support log purge APIs and compliance deletion flows; we'll include that in the compliance pack we send.
[06:45] Laura Gomez: what about dev debugging? sometimes we need to see raw interactions to tune prompts.
[06:51] Maya Chen: recommended approach: provide a redacted sample or use ephemeral debug mode for a short window with strict access controls; all debug data can be set to auto-delete after X hours.
[07:07] Sofia Marin: any legal paperwork before we start? DPA, security addendum?
[07:12] Maya Chen: yes we will route the DPA and standard security addendum; for Dedicated/Private we have additional language around deployment and key ownership.
[07:23] Dr. Amit Rao: can we get an explicit statement on whether prompts are used to improve Redwood models?
[07:29] Maya Chen: we do not use customer prompts to train public models. for hosted customers there is an option to opt out of any data use for service improvement; Dedicated/Private defaults to no training use.
[07:44] Arjun Patel: back to benchmarks — we'll gather sample payload sizes; please include typical length distribution and percent of long prompts.
[07:54] Laura Gomez: distribution: 60% short (<=50 tokens), 30% medium (50–200), 10% long (>200). peak minutes are 2–3pm PST.
[08:06] Arjun Patel: good, that helps sizing. expected token per request around 120 average.
[08:12] Maya Chen: for acceptance testing, we will run 3 runs with cold start and warm start scenarios and capture p50/p95, errors, and cost.
[08:25] Sofia Marin: will you provide the exact locust/jmeter script?
[08:29] Arjun Patel: yes will share in GitHub and a quick runbook.
[08:34] Terry Huang: about monitoring — we need traces linked to requests but without PII. can you redact in traces?
[08:40] Jordan Li: traces can be configured to remove or hash fields; we'll provide recommended trace scrubbing rules that match your PII list.
[08:52] Laura Gomez: ok next steps?
[08:55] Maya Chen: we'll share docs (security + KMS), benchmark script, and pricing. you to share sample datasets and PII rules. then we schedule kickoff.
[09:05] Dr. Amit Rao: sounds good. anything else on timeline?
[09:09] Maya Chen: aim to start provisioning Dedicated infra by 2026-07-20 pending contract; kickoff week of 2026-07-27.
[09:20] Sofia Marin: one more thing — can we flag a list of fields we never want stored even in ephemeral logs?
[09:26] Maya Chen: yes add that to the PII doc and we'll enforce masking at ingest.
[09:33] Laura Gomez: thanks all.
[09:36] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the bundle of docs and a draft SOW.
[09:44] (call ends)
notes: Customer prefers Dedicated for the POC due to PHI concerns; agreed acceptance criteria and 4-week pilot plan. Redwood to provide security/compliance docs, benchmark scripts, and pricing. Customer to provide sample datasets and PII redaction guidance.
proposed_pilot_timeline: Week 0: prep & data exchange; Week 1: infra setup + small benchmark; Week 2: full benchmark and tuning; Week 3: evaluation, report & decision
acceptance_criteria: 1) latency p50 <300ms p95 <900ms on small profile; 2) throughput target: 1k concurrent requests sustained for 15 mins without errors; 3) redaction policy enforced (no stored PHI in hosted logs); 4) quality regression <=5% on golden prompts
benchmark_profile_summary: Small: 4k requests over 1 hour, avg 40 tokens; Heavy: bursty 1k rpm, avg 200 tokens; metrics: tokens/sec, p95 latency, error rate, cost/1k tokens
special_constraints: Must not persist raw PHI in hosted logs; support CMK via KMS; audit export required; ability to purge records on request
